title: Check Before You Drop

patient.name: Mr Subramaniam s/o Rajaratnam
patient.presenting_complaint: First visit, referred for blurring of vision for 2 days; doctor has ordered dilation for fundus examination

history.hpc: Mr Subramaniam says 'Doctor want to open up my eye to check the back, is it? Two days my eye blur already.' This is his first visit. He declined the near vision test earlier. Importantly, he tells you 'I allergic to one of the eye drop — the one that make eye big, Phenylephrine.' Following the first eye examination, the doctor has ordered the patient's eyes to be dilated for a fundus examination, and Goldmann applanation tonometry has been done.
history.pmhx: First visit. Known allergy to Phenylephrine eye drops. No other allergies stated.
history.family_hx: To be elicited as part of the assessment
medications: To be confirmed; note the Phenylephrine allergy

examination_findings.anterior_segment: For doctor review; no contraindication to dilation noted by the doctor who ordered it
examination_findings.fundus: To be examined by the doctor after dilation

investigations.allergy_check: Patient reports allergy to Phenylephrine — this must be confirmed and acted upon: Phenylephrine-containing dilating drops must NOT be instilled
investigations.dilation_plan: Use a dilating regimen that avoids Phenylephrine (e.g. Tropicamide alone, or as directed by the doctor/protocol for a Phenylephrine-allergic patient); confirm with the nurse/doctor before instilling
investigations.gat_done: Goldmann applanation tonometry already performed: right 18 mmHg, left 20 mmHg
investigations.instillation_method: Aseptic, no-touch instillation into the lower fornix with correct positioning and post-instillation advice

diagnosis: Dilation prepared safely for fundus examination. The critical step is recognising and acting on the patient's Phenylephrine allergy: Phenylephrine-containing drops are withheld and an alternative dilating agent is used or confirmed with the doctor before instillation. Identity, consent, allergy confirmation and correct instillation technique are completed, and the patient is advised about temporary blurred near vision and light sensitivity after dilation. The PSA does not make a medical diagnosis.

immediate: Confirm patient identity using two identifiers and confirm the doctor's order to dilate
Confirm the allergy: the patient is allergic to Phenylephrine — do NOT instil any Phenylephrine-containing dilating drop
Select/confirm an appropriate alternative dilating drop (e.g. Tropicamide alone) and check with the nurse/doctor or protocol before instilling
Explain the purpose of dilation and that vision will be blurred and light-sensitive for a few hours; obtain consent
Perform hand hygiene; check drop label, strength and expiry and confirm the correct drop and eye(s)
Instil the drop into the lower fornix using a no-touch technique, then apply gentle punctal occlusion / give a tissue
Document the allergy, the drug withheld, the drug given, time, eye(s) and that GAT was completed before dilation
follow_up: Inform the doctor that dilation has been instilled and note the time so the fundus exam is done when adequately dilated
Monitor for any allergic or adverse reaction and report immediately
Advise the patient not to drive until the dilation wears off and to wait for review
patient_education: Explain why the eye is being dilated (to let the doctor see the back of the eye)
Warn about temporary blurred near vision and sensitivity to light, and to avoid driving until it wears off
Reassure the patient that the Phenylephrine allergy has been noted and avoided

key_points: Confirms identity with two identifiers and confirms the order to dilate
Actively confirms drug allergy and identifies the Phenylephrine allergy
Explains the purpose and effects of dilation and obtains consent
Confirms which eye(s) are to be dilated
Withholds Phenylephrine-containing drops because of the allergy
Selects/confirms an appropriate alternative dilating agent with the doctor/protocol
Checks drop label, strength, expiry and correct eye before instilling
Uses an aseptic, no-touch instillation technique into the lower fornix
Recognises the allergy check as the critical safety step before dilation
Understands the purpose of dilation for fundus examination
Knows that GAT/IOP is typically measured before dilation
Does not make a medical diagnosis — acts within the PSA role
Documents the allergy, drug withheld, drug given, eye and time clearly
Applies punctal occlusion and gives post-dilation safety advice (no driving, light sensitivity)
Monitors for and would report any adverse reaction
Communicates the dilation time to the doctor for the fundus exam
